project.name: stable-range
project.description: Bass stable-range conditions for finite right-unimodular rows, quotient and local-ring consequences, regular and unit-regular rings, categorical biproduct cancellation and module cancellation, division-ring matrix row rank and repeated blocks, commutative dimension bounds, kernel-product decompositions with specified sections over semirings, arbitrary-ring right-coefficient row splittings and rectangular completion from free right kernels, commutative free coefficient-row kernels, explicit two-element row completion and supplied-product cancellation, exact-size finite-free cancellation and first-row completion, and elementary diagonalization over commutative rings satisfying Bass S_1, with determinant-one generation and the stable elementary quotient. A commutative ring with finite maximal spectrum satisfies S_1. Idempotent corners of arbitrary rings satisfying S_1 also satisfy S_1. Division semirings are local and have zero nonunits additive submonoid. In a commutative local semiring, the additive view of the maximal ideal is the submonoid of nonunits. In a possibly noncommutative local ring, every proper left ideal lies in the Jacobson radical, which is the unique maximal left ideal. Conversely, a ring is local exactly when its canonical Jacobson radical is maximal among all left ideals; properness supplies nontriviality. General rings need not be commutative; commutative and division-ring results retain their separate hypotheses.

headlines.text:
These results use Mathlib. The quasiregular-ideal predicate and unit characterization
come from pinned `general-linear-groups`; the stable-range consequences are proved
here. The [guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/docs/GUIDE.md#headline-results) retains detailed statements,
coordinate formulas, compatibility names and client inventories.

headlines.title: Bass conditions
headlines.text:
**[Bass conditions](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Basic.lean).** For arbitrary possibly noncommutative rings: right-unimodular
rows, `(S_n)`, least stable index, monotonicity, ring-equivalence invariance and
[surjective descent/quasiregular quotients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Quotient.lean).
[Nontrivial local rings](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Local.lean) have least stable range one.

headlines.title: Local interfaces
headlines.text:
**Local interfaces.** [Division semirings](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Local.lean) are local with
zero nonunits submonoid; the maximal-ideal additive comparison requires a
commutative local semiring.
For rings, locality is equivalent to Jacobson-radical maximality among all left
ideals. In local rings the radical is the nonunits and contains every proper
left ideal; these statements do not assume two-sidedness of the left ideals.

headlines.title: Preservation
headlines.text:
**Preservation.** [Products](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Product.lean) preserve every `(S_n)`.
[Semisimple rings and semisimple radical quotients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Semisimple.lean)
satisfy `(S₁)` without radical nilpotence. [Finite matrix rings](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Matrix.lean),
[idempotent corners](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Corner.lean) and [opposites](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Opposite.lean)
preserve `(S₁)`; matrix reflection needs nonempty indices, corners neither
centrality nor fullness. [Commutative semilocal rings](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Semilocal.lean)
satisfy `(S₁)` assuming only finite maximal spectrum, including the zero ring.

headlines.title: Retract endomorphisms
headlines.text:
**[Retract endomorphisms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/CategoryTheory/EndRetract.lean).**
In any preadditive category, `i : X ⟶ Z`, `p : Z ⟶ X` and `i ≫ p = 𝟙 X`
transfer `Bass.StableRangeCondition (End Z) 1` to
`Bass.StableRangeCondition (End X) 1` for the original canonical endomorphism
rings. Object and morphism universes are independent; no complementary object,
finite-length or nonzero hypothesis is needed.

headlines.title: Finite biproduct endomorphisms
headlines.text:
**[Finite biproduct endomorphisms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/CategoryTheory/FiniteLocalEnd.lean).**
In any preadditive category, a displayed finite biproduct of objects with local
endomorphism rings, and every displayed retract of that biproduct, have canonical
endomorphism rings satisfying `(S₁)`. Only that biproduct and, for the retract,
its supplied retraction are required, with independent index universe; empty
families and the zero biproduct are included. No vanishing of morphisms between
summands is assumed.

headlines.title: Regularity and cancellation
headlines.text:
**Regularity and cancellation.** [`(S₁)`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Regular.lean) implies direct
finiteness, is equivalent to unit-valued pair shortening, and under von Neumann
regularity is equivalent to unit-regularity.
[Biproduct cancellation](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/CategoryTheory/Cancellation.lean) in any
preadditive category needs `(S₁)` for the canonical `End(X)` and only the two
displayed biproducts. The remaining objects are unrestricted; local End is
sufficient, and neither global sums nor commutativity is assumed.
[Module cancellation](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Cancellation.lean) is a specialization,
with independent carrier universes and no finiteness or projectivity;
regular right modules use the opposite ring. [Division-ring vector-space endomorphisms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/DivisionRing.lean)
have inner inverses; finite dimension gives automorphic inner inverses and
unit-regular finite matrix rings, including empty indices.

headlines.title: Ranks and blocks
headlines.text:
**Ranks and blocks.** [Division-ring row rank](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/DivisionRingRank.lean)
has rectangular bounds, reindexing, realization and repeated-block laws;
normalized empty square rank is zero. [Repeated-block homomorphisms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/RepeatedBlock.lean)
work over `NonAssocSemiring` coefficients, injectively for nonempty block families.

headlines.title: Commutative dimension bounds
headlines.text:
**Commutative dimension bounds.** [Regularity](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Commutative.lean) is
equivalent to reducedness and dimension at most zero; all modules over such
regular rings are flat.
[Dimension at most zero gives `(S₁)`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/CommutativeStableRange.lean)
without reducedness or nontriviality; commutative regular rings are unit-regular.
[Noetherian dimension at most `d` gives `(S_(d+1))`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/BassDimension.lean),
with no infinite-residue-fields premise.

headlines.title: Specified splittings
headlines.text:
**Specified splittings.** [A supplied linear right inverse of a linear map `f`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Module/SplitSurjective.lean)
gives `ker f × N ≃ₗ[R] M` over a semiring, for an additive commutative group `M`
and additive commutative monoid `N`, in independent universes. The prescribed
complementary endomorphism `id - g.comp f` has range exactly `ker f`.
[Complementary-range ranks](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/Module/SplitSurjectiveRank.lean) over a
division ring satisfy `finrank K (range (id - g.comp f)) = finrank K M - finrank K N`
assuming only that `M` is finite-dimensional. A family with given equivalences
`N b ≃ₗ[K] F` has this rank equal to `finrank K M - finrank K F` at every `b`,
without a nonempty base or a finite-dimensionality assumption on `F`.
[Right-unimodular
coefficient rows](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/RowKernel.lean) split over `Rᵐᵒᵖ` for any ring, including empty
rows and the zero ring. Splitting alone does not give freeness.

headlines.title: Completion and IBN
headlines.text:
**Completion and IBN.** [Right-unimodularity and free right kernels](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/RightRowCompletion.lean)
characterize two-sided rectangular completion, preserving a supplied inverse
column. For successor-length rows, [square completion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/SquareRightRowCompletionCriterion.lean)
needs IBN only to infer kernel size; supplied matching coordinates and the
converse need no IBN. The [countable endomorphism example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/CountableEndomorphism.lean)
separates rectangular from square completion for nontrivial underlying modules,
even for a unary row.

headlines.title: Commutative cancellation
headlines.text:
**Commutative cancellation.** Under `(S_s)`, right-unimodular rows of length at
least `s + 1` have free kernels. [Finite-free cancellation](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/FiniteFree.lean) uses an
explicit `P × R^m ≃ R^(n+m)` and `s ≤ n`, without prior freeness of `P`;
[completion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/RowCompletion.lean) preserves the literal first row.
Both allow zero rings; dimension-bound variants require Noetherianity.
[Two-entry completion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/RowCompletionTwo.lean) retains supplied Bézout
coefficients over commutative rings, with explicit scalar kernel coordinates.

headlines.title: Elementary matrices and determinants
headlines.text:
**Elementary matrices and determinants.** For commutative rings satisfying `(S₁)`,
[elementary diagonalization](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/ElementaryGeneration.lean) works in all
finite ranks, including zero. [Determinant generation](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/stable-range/blob/4d01f17954ba77e8ec53cf1524c9057e8f3d72e3/StableRange/DeterminantGeneration.lean)
identifies invertible determinant-one matrices with elementary matrices, the stable
elementary subgroup with the determinant kernel, and its quotient with units,
without locality, nontriviality or positive-rank hypotheses.

main_results.name: Bass.StableRangeCondition
main_results.note: Bass S_n uses finite right-unimodular rows with witness coefficients on the right; IsStableRange is a relational least natural index, not a default value when no finite bound exists.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_one_of_finite_maximalSpectrum
main_results.note: Under CommRing and finite maximal spectrum, the proved S_1 condition shortens the second entry of a right-unimodular pair by b - a*t, including the zero ring.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_one_corner
main_results.note: For any idempotent e in a possibly noncommutative ring satisfying S_1, Mathlib's corner eRe with identity e also satisfies S_1. Neither centrality, fullness nor nontriviality is required.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_mono
main_results.note: S_m implies S_n for m <= n, over arbitrary possibly noncommutative rings.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_of_surjective
main_results.note: Stable-range conditions descend along surjective ring homomorphisms.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_quotient_iff
main_results.note: Quotienting by a quasiregular two-sided ideal preserves every S_n; reflection is not asserted for arbitrary quotient ideals.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRange_one_of_isLocalRing
main_results.note: A native possibly noncommutative local ring has least stable range one. The native local-ring hypotheses exclude the zero ring.

main_results.name: IsLocalRing.le_ringJacobson
main_results.note: Every proper left ideal of a possibly noncommutative local ring lies in its Jacobson radical, without a two-sidedness hypothesis. Locality includes nontriviality.

main_results.name: IsLocalRing.isMaximal_iff_eq_ringJacobson
main_results.note: In any possibly noncommutative local ring, a left ideal is maximal exactly when it is the Jacobson radical. The radical is maximal, and every maximal left ideal is identified with this same ideal; no two-sidedness hypothesis is imposed. Locality includes nontriviality.

main_results.name: IsLocalRing.of_ringJacobson_isMaximal
main_results.note: For any possibly noncommutative ring, maximality of its canonical Jacobson radical among all left ideals supplies unit-theoretic locality. No locality or separate nontriviality premise is required; maximality includes properness.

main_results.name: IsLocalRing.iff_ringJacobson_isMaximal
main_results.note: A ring is local exactly when its canonical Jacobson radical is maximal among all left ideals, not only two-sided ideals. This ring criterion does not subsume Mathlib's commutative-semiring unique-maximal-ideal provider.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_one_isDedekindFinite
main_results.note: S_1 makes every one-sided inverse two-sided.

main_results.name: Bass.isUnitRegular_iff_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: For a von Neumann-regular ring, unit-regularity is equivalent to S_1. Replacing S_1 by least stable range one additionally requires Nontrivial.

main_results.name: Bass.principalRightIdeals_isCompl_of_innerInverse
main_results.note: An inner inverse x for a gives complementary aR and (1-a*x)R, represented as submodules over the opposite ring.

main_results.name: Bass.not_isUnitRegular_moduleEnd_finsupp_nat
main_results.note: The endomorphism ring of a countable direct sum of copies of any nonzero additive module is not unit-regular. Neither the coefficient module nor this direct sum is asserted to be free.

main_results.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_iso_of_biprod_iso_of_end_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: In a preadditive category with independent object and Hom universes, S_1 for the canonical End(X) makes X cancel from X biprod Y isomorphic to X biprod Z. Only those two biproducts are required, with no restrictions on Y or Z. The End ring need not be commutative or nontrivial. This generalizes the existing module cancellation proof.

main_results.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_iso_of_biprod_iso_of_isLocalRing_end
main_results.note: A possibly noncommutative local endomorphism ring supplies S_1 and hence biproduct cancellation with the same two-sum floor.

main_results.name: Bass.exists_linearEquiv_of_prod_of_end_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: If End_R(M) satisfies S_1, an equivalence M x A = M x B gives an equivalence A = B, with no finiteness or projectivity hypothesis. This is a specialization of categorical cancellation, retaining all independent scalar and carrier universes.

main_results.name: Bass.IsUnitRegular.subsingleton_of_fin_linearEquiv_fin_prod
main_results.note: Finite powers of the regular right module over a unit-regular ring cannot absorb a nontrivial complementary module, including power zero.

main_results.name: Bass.isVonNeumannRegular_moduleEnd
main_results.note: The endomorphism ring of any vector space over a division ring is regular.

main_results.name: Bass.isUnitRegular_matrix
main_results.note: Every finite square matrix ring over a division ring is unit-regular, including the empty index case; finite dimension supplies automorphic inner inverses, unlike the arbitrary-vector-space assertion.

main_results.name: Matrix.repeatBlockHom
main_results.note: Repeating square matrices on finite diagonal blocks is a ring homomorphism at NonAssocSemiring generality. Its value is Kronecker product with an identity; injectivity needs a nonempty block family.

main_results.name: Matrix.rowRank
main_results.note: Finrank of the range of the left-linear row-vector map given by right multiplication, over a possibly noncommutative division ring. The API includes multiplication bounds, reindex invariance and additivity on mutually orthogonal idempotents.

main_results.name: Matrix.exists_rowRank_eq
main_results.note: Every natural rank bounded by the finite square size is realized.

main_results.name: Matrix.rowRank_repeatBlock
main_results.note: Repeated blocks scale row rank by their number, including an empty block family.

main_results.name: Matrix.normalizedRowRank_repeatBlock
main_results.note: Normalized real rank is preserved for nonempty square matrices and nonempty finite block families. Normalized rank of the identity is one only under the nonempty-size hypothesis; empty-size division is totalized in Lean and does not give that assertion.

main_results.name: Bass.isVonNeumannRegular_iff_isReduced_and_krullDimLE_zero
main_results.note: Commutative regular rings are exactly reduced rings of Krull dimension at most zero.

main_results.name: Bass.IsVonNeumannRegular.flat
main_results.note: Every module over a commutative regular ring is flat, with no finite-generation assumption.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_one_of_krullDimLE_zero
main_results.note: Krull dimension at most zero implies S_1 for commutative rings, without reducedness or nontriviality. The separate least-index-one result requires Nontrivial; the zero ring satisfies S_0.

main_results.name: Bass.IsVonNeumannRegular.isUnitRegular
main_results.note: Every commutative regular ring is unit-regular.

main_results.name: Bass.stableRangeCondition_succ_of_krullDimLE
main_results.note: A commutative noetherian ring of Krull dimension at most d satisfies S_(d+1). No reducedness, nontriviality or infinite-residue-field assumption is imposed; the proof uses finite-prime avoidance and height.

main_results.name: LinearMap.kerProdEquivOfRightInverse
main_results.note: Over a semiring, a specified linear right inverse gives ker(f) x N equivalent to the additive-group source M, with additive-monoid target N and independent universes. Forward coordinates add the kernel element to the section image; inverse coordinates are x - s(f(x)) and f(x). Neither finiteness, projectivity nor freeness is required.

main_results.name: LinearMap.kerProdEquivOfRightInverse_ofInjective
main_results.note: Under the ring hypotheses of Mathlib's right-split-exact equivalence, identifying any injective first map with the kernel transports the kernel-product equivalence to that construction using the same section.

main_results.name: LinearMap.isRightUnimodular_iff_surjective_dotProductBilin
main_results.note: For any ring R and finite row a, the right-linear map over Rᵐᵒᵖ evaluates to sum a_i*x_i. Right-unimodularity is equivalent to its surjectivity; companion section and right-span criteria include the empty row and the zero ring.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.rightCoefficientKernelProd
main_results.note: A right-inverse column b gives the section y ↦ (b_i*y) and an explicit right-linear equivalence ker(σ) × R ≃ R^n whose inverse second coordinate is the original row σ. No free kernel or matrix completion follows from this arbitrary-ring splitting.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.rightCoefficientRowCoordinates
main_results.note: A chosen right-inverse column and finite coordinates of the right kernel give a right-linear equivalence whose first coordinate is the original row and whose tail is the chosen coordinate of its witness-dependent kernel projection.

main_results.name: Matrix.rightRowCompletion
main_results.note: The supplied witness and kernel coordinates yield a rectangular matrix with first row equal to the original row, paired with an explicit two-sided inverse that retains the supplied witness as its first column. Matrix actions agree with the coordinate maps.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.rightCoefficientKernelEquivOfMatrixInverse
main_results.note: A two-sided rectangular inverse with specified first row gives actual right-kernel coordinates by tail(A *ᵥ k), reconstructed by B *ᵥ Fin.cons 0 t; no prior freeness assumption is required.

main_results.name: Matrix.isRightUnimodular_and_free_kernel_iff_exists_rectangular_inverse
main_results.note: Over any ring, right-unimodularity with a free right kernel is equivalent to some finite rectangular two-sided inverse pair retaining the row. Splitting derives finite generation of the kernel; no commutativity, stable-range or invariant-basis-number condition is imposed.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.isRightUnimodular_iff_exists_kernelProdEquiv
main_results.note: A finite row is right-unimodular exactly when it has a kernel-product equivalence over the opposite ring with inverse second coordinate equal to the original row, not just an abstract product equivalence.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.kernelProdEquivOfIsRightUnimodular_eq_rightCoefficientKernelProd
main_results.note: For commutative rings, kernel transport compares the scalar and right-linear splittings using the same chosen witness in both; the comparison does not identify that witness with a test fixture.

main_results.name: Bass.coefficientRowKernelEquivSuccOfStableRangeCondition
main_results.note: Over a commutative ring satisfying S_n, a right-unimodular row of length n+1 has kernel explicitly equivalent to the free module on Fin n. Monotonicity gives free kernels for lengths at least s+1 under S_s, without Noetherianity or a dimension bound.

main_results.name: Bass.coefficientRowKernelEquivOfMatrixInverse
main_results.note: Over a commutative ring, any chosen row i of a matrix with a specified two-sided inverse has kernel equivalent to functions on the other indices. No stable-range assumption is used; i : Fin n supplies nonemptiness and n=1 gives the empty complementary index type.

main_results.name: Matrix.coefficientRowCompletionTwo
main_results.note: Over any commutative ring, a specified witness a₀b₀+a₁b₁=1 completes the row (a₀,a₁) to a determinant-one matrix with second row (-b₁,b₀). Its inverse has rows (b₀,-a₁) and (b₁,a₀).

main_results.name: Bass.coefficientRowKernelEquivTwo
main_results.note: The supplied completion identifies the kernel of the original two-element coefficient functional with R, with coordinate -b₁x₀+b₀x₁ and inverse generator (-a₁t,a₀t).

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.coefficientProductCancellationTwo
main_results.note: Any supplied (Fin 2 → R) ≃ₗ[R] (R × P) over a commutative ring identifies P ≃ₗ[R] R via its original first projection and kernel; no stable-range, freeness or nontriviality hypothesis is required.

main_results.name: Module.finLinearEquivOfStableRangeCondition
main_results.note: For a commutative R satisfying S_s, an explicit equivalence P x R^m = R^(n+m) with s <= n yields P = R^n, with the exact coordinate count, independent module universe and zero ring allowed. The noetherian Krull-dimension-bound specialization has separate hypotheses.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.coefficientRowCompletionOfStableRangeCondition
main_results.note: A right-unimodular row of length n+1 over a commutative ring satisfying S_s with s <= n yields a self-equivalence whose first output coordinate is the original coefficient functional. Its matrix has that first row and the same specified inverse satisfies both inverse identities.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.exists_elementary_unit_pivot_of_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: Bass S_1 over a commutative ring yields an elementary left factor with a unit leading entry for every invertible successor-rank matrix, including rank one and the zero ring; locality is not required.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.exists_elementary_diagonalization_of_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: Two-sided elementary factors diagonalize every invertible Fin n matrix into units under commutative S_1, including the empty matrix. The generic all-rank unit-pivot induction comes from general-linear-groups.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.exists_elementary_diagonalization_finite_of_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: The same diagonalization transports along a finite equivalence to any finite decidable index type, without a chosen order or Nontrivial.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.mem_elementarySubgroup_iff_det_eq_one_of_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: Over a commutative S_1 ring, an invertible matrix at any finite decidable index type is elementary exactly when its determinant is one; the empty index type and the zero ring are included.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.StableGL.elementary_eq_ker_det_of_stableRangeCondition_one
main_results.note: The stable elementary subgroup is the kernel of the stable determinant, by reducing a stable representative to a finite stage.

main_results.name: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.StableGL.quotientDetMulEquivOfStableRangeConditionOne
main_results.note: The stable elementary quotient is equivalent to the coefficient units; the forward map is the quotient determinant and the inverse is the existing rank-one section.
